messages.content: Find the working hours and ticket price of The British Museum for this weekend, Jun.20,2023.

function.name: museum_info
function.description: Get information about a museum including its opening hours and ticket prices for a specific date range. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

date.description: The specific date for which information is needed, in the format of YYYY-MM-DD such as '2022-12-01'.

information.description: The type of information needed from the museum. This is optional and defaults to 'all' if not specified.

message.reasoning:
The user wants the working hours and ticket price of The British Museum for this weekend, Jun.20,2023. They want the working hours and ticket price. The date is Jun.20,2023. The user says "this weekend" but they also specify Jun.20,2023. That is a Saturday. So we need to get the working hours and ticket price for that date. We can use the function "museum_info" with museum="The British Museum", date="2023-06-20", information=["opening_hours","ticket_price"]. The function expects "information" to be an array of strings? The type says "information?: "opening_hours" | "ticket_price" | "address"[], // default: "all"". Actually the type says "information?: "opening_hours" | "ticket_price" | "address"[], // default: "all"". That seems ambiguous. It might mean that "information" can be one of those strings or an array of those strings. But the example says "information?: "opening_hours" | "ticket_price" | "address"[], // default: "all"". That might be a mistake. But we can pass an array: ["opening_hours","ticket_price"].

We should call the function.
